At Instructure , we believe in the power of people to grow and succeed throughout their lives. Our goal is to amplify that power by creating intuitive products that simplify learning and personal development, facilitate meaningful relationships, and inspire people to go further in their education and careers.
We do this by giving smart, creative, passionate people opportunities to create awesome. And that's where you come in:
Foundry is a new division inside Instructure, built to generate new revenue with AI-built products. We operate as a portfolio of small pods, each charged with one product bet, under tight weekly governance. They operate independently, with dedicated resources, separate from the core business on purpose: different pace, different governance, and different rewards.
Our goal is to generate meaningful revenue within 12 to 18 months, so this isn’t an innovation lab. We’re building scaled businesses that customers pay for and retain well, and we’re measuring ourselves on revenue, not activity.
Instructure reaches roughly half of higher education in the United States, connecting a credential network of more than 13,000 institutions. Pair that distribution and data with a fast-moving team that builds leanly, and you have something no competitor has. That’s the opportunity New Markets exists to take.
How we work
A pod is two people: a Founder and a Builder, both hands on, close to the customer. The bet is deliberate: we invest in agent-developer tooling and tokens, not in headcount. An operating team of growth marketing, revenue operations, sales overlay, and G&A supports every pod, so founders stay on building products.
Every pod inherits an underlying platform with common design, development, and deployment harnesses, so no pod rebuilds the plumbing. Each pod runs through key phases with regular checkpoints where a governing board reviews progress or recommends a pivot or kill.
The rhythm is fast and transparent. Investor-style updates go out weekly. Demos and keep-or-kill checkpoints happen twice a month. Transparency is the operating model.

You’re the operational engine behind New Markets’ newest product bets. You’ll own the end-to-end go-to-market lifecycle for pod products, from market sizing and early strategy through launch, performance tracking, and the handoff when a product graduates into the core.

When a pod proves customers will pay, you make that motion repeatable and hand it to the full seller base. This is a blank-page job: the playbook doesn’t exist yet, and you’ll write it. The role reports directly to the President, New Markets, with a matrixed dotted line to Instructure’s Go-to-Market Strategy and Operations leadership.
What you’ll own
You own go-to-market operations across the portfolio, and you’re the voice of the New Markets business in the rooms where commercial decisions get made.

Own the end-to-end GTM lifecycle for pod products. Carry each product from market sizing and early strategy through launch planning, field execution, and post-launch performance tracking.
Shape the go-to-market approach with each pod. Partner with Pod Founders, marketing, and the sales overlay on ideal-customer definition, pricing and packaging input, channel strategy, and competitive positioning.
Design the sales motion. Build the coverage models, pipeline processes, forecasting cadences, and rules of engagement for the first seller cohort on each product.
Build the reporting backbone. Stand up and maintain the analytics in Salesforce and Excel that track pipeline health, win/loss, attach rates, average contract value, and renewal trends, and turn that data into insight leadership can act on.
Run launch readiness. Lead CRM buildout in Salesforce, playbook documentation, tool configuration, and alignment across enablement, marketing, finance, deal desk, and IT.
Own the graduation playbook. Define the criteria and the integration motion for products that complete a pod’s journey, so the full seller base can carry and sell the product without a messy handoff.
Be the voice of the business. Translate early-stage complexity into clear, data-backed narratives in planning forums, business reviews, and executive sessions, and support annual planning across capacity, quota, incentive design, and growth roadmaps.
What we expect
Blank page to operating framework. You go from nothing to a working system without a lot of hand-holding, then improve it as results and field feedback come in.
Rigor under ambiguity. You structure messy, early-stage go-to-market problems, build the analytical frame, and land a recommendation you can defend.
Accuracy you stand behind. The insights and reporting you put in front of leadership are right, and you own them.
Influence without authority. You move product, finance, marketing, and sales toward a shared plan without managing any of them.

Five or more years in sales operations, revenue operations, or a related go-to-market function.
Real experience supporting new-product launches or emerging-business initiatives, where the playbook didn’t exist yet.
Three or more years hands-on in Salesforce, building and maintaining reports, dashboards, and data structures.
Advanced Excel, comfortable building models, running variance analysis, and turning raw data into decision-ready output.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive-level presentations. A bachelor’s degree is preferred.
Your first 90 days
Month 1. Immerse yourself in the New Markets portfolio, the key stakeholders, and the current go-to-market infrastructure. Understand where each product sits in its lifecycle and find the most pressing operational gaps.
Month 3. Establish a clear view of performance across active pods: pipeline health, coverage, and leading indicators. Build or refine the reporting framework in Salesforce and Excel, and set a recurring operating rhythm with product and sales leadership.
Month 6. Own and drive the go-to-market motion for at least one pod through a checkpoint. Deliver an integration-readiness recommendation for any product approaching graduation, and present a prioritized roadmap for improving New Markets go-to-market operations to senior leadership.
This role isn’t for everyone

About Neon
Neon is a global payments and e-commerce platform designed to help game publishers earn more money and independence from app stores. We believe commerce should be open and transparent: clear decisions, actionable insights, and aligned incentives.

Founded by payments, fintech and gaming veterans, Neon focuses on product and partnership excellence: we share the playbook, co-pilot decisions, and abstract away risk and complexity for our customers. We’re replacing old-school, black-box relics with clear, modern, and developer-centric infrastructure.
As an early team member, you’ll have the opportunity to shape and scale Neon’s product and culture, making a direct impact on our growth and success. You’ll join a collaborative, diverse team from world-class companies like Apple, Affirm, Unity, and Visa, backed by renowned VC's including Thrive, a16z, Griffin Gaming, Ribbit, and Renegade. If you want to build disruptive technology, challenge the status quo, and help game creators thrive on their own terms, read on.

Neon is a gaming-focused Merchant of Record platform serving game publishers globally. We process payments across 50+ markets through multiple PSPs simultaneously, operating as the seller of record across card networks, local wallets, A2A rails, and alternative payment methods.
This role owns the operational backbone of that system: dispute and chargeback management, fraud operations, compliance monitoring, payment performance tracking, and operational support for Customer Success.

As the senior operator across these functions, the Payment Operations Manager sets operational standards, defines targets, owns PSP and partner operational relationships, and is accountable for outcomes across payments, risk, fraud, and compliance.

The role partners with the Head of Payments and the Risk, Fraud & Compliance Product Leader as a peer across all four functions.
This is a senior individual-contributor role . The Manager title reflects the seniority and ownership scope of the role and function, not direct reports at this stage.

Dispute & Chargeback Operations
Own dispute intake, evidence compilation, and resolution across all active payment processors and markets.
Define and own resolution SLAs and win-rate targets; identify systemic patterns and drive fixes with product and risk leads.
Prioritize and drive the roadmap for internal dispute tooling as operational infrastructure matures.
Fraud Operations
Own fraud operations and oversee investigations and transaction reviews in partnership with the Risk, Fraud & Compliance Product Leader.
Set monitoring and escalation standards across screening and decisioning tools; maintain case integrity and decision quality.
Track fraud loss trends across markets and game titles; surface and act on emerging attack patterns before they scale.
Payment Performance Monitoring
Own tracking of authorization rates, payment success rates, decline codes, and fraud losses across processors and markets.
Own post-launch metric reviews for new payment methods against defined performance thresholds.
Define the operational dashboard and alerting standard; ensure anomalies are caught before they become publisher-impacting incidents.
Customer Success Support
Serve as the senior operational point of contact for payment-related requests escalated by Customer Success.
Lead deep dives into publisher payment performance, dispute trends, and fraud exposure, producing structured analysis CS can use directly in publisher conversations.
Own the operational response to payment incidents: root cause investigation, timeline reconstruction, and remediation communication.
PSP & Partner Management
Own day-to-day operational relationships with PSPs and payment partners, including performance reviews, escalations, and issue resolution.
Hold partners accountable to performance and SLA commitments; drive improvement where markets or methods underperform.
Process, Tooling & Standards
Set and maintain operational standards, runbooks, and process documentation that others follow.
Prioritize automation opportunities and partner with the Head of Payments, Risk & Compliance, and engineering to translate operational gaps into product and tooling improvements.
Act as the senior escalation point for payment operations.
Key Success Metrics
Dispute win rate and resolution turnaround, owned and improved per processor.
Fraud operations outcomes: fraud loss rate, false positive rate, detection rate, and escalation accuracy.
PSR performance against target across active payment methods and markets, with defined review triggers on all methods.
Incident response and resolution time for publisher-impacting payment issues.
Reporting accuracy, on-time delivery, and operational process maturity as the function scales.
Ideal Profile
6-8+ years in payments operations, fraud ops, or fintech risk, with a track record of owning a function or leading operational initiatives, ideally at a PSP, Merchant of Record, or digital goods company.
Has run these functions end to end, not just participated in them; comfortable operating across multiple payment processors simultaneously, with direct experience of global PSPs such as Stripe, Adyen, PayPal, or Razorpay.
Experience owning PSP or partner relationships and influencing product, engineering, and Customer Success without formal authority.
Deep understanding of dispute and chargeback mechanics at the card network level (Visa/Mastercard rules), not just tool navigation.
Strong analytical capability: works across dashboards and data tools, builds structured reports, and finds signals in noisy transaction data.
Detail-oriented and self-directing; operates with significant autonomy across a broad and growing operational surface.
Business-level English proficiency required, written and verbal.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Alongside our model releases, Anthropic ships a steady stream of launches across the rest of the portfolio — products like Claude, Claude Code, and the developer platform; solutions for enterprises and startups; and the safeguards work that keeps Claude safe and trustworthy. Each launch brings product, engineering, policy, legal, communications, sales, and every part of marketing together around a single moment.
You'll be the central organizer of the product launch process for the product marketing team. You'll build and run the operating system behind it: the launch calendar, the plan of record for every deliverable, the path materials take through review, and execution on launch day. You'll treat the launch process itself as a product and drive adoption through influence.
In a portfolio this broad, not everything can get the same attention, so you'll focus your time on the team's top priorities, putting the most energy behind the launches that matter most and keeping the rest running on the systems you've built.
This is a hands-on, high-ownership role on a lean product marketing team. When launch volume peaks, you'll contribute directly as a product marketer across all products and surfaces. If you've run launches where many moving parts had to converge at the same time, and you'd rather design the system than run it by hand, we'd like to meet you.

Serve as one of the core organizers of the product launch process end to end: collaborating with peers across product, operations, and GTM
Own the product launch calendar and sequencing across a broad portfolio of releases — products, solutions, and programs — prioritizing your time against the team's top priorities and coordinating timing with partner teams across marketing, product, and communications
Own the plan of record for each launch, like deliverables, owners, dependencies, and deadlines, and surface risks early enough to act on them
Own the path launch materials take through review, partnering with legal, policy, product, and communications so reviews happen in the right sequence against dates people can plan to
Drive decisions and alignment across senior cross-functional stakeholders without direct authority
Own launch-day execution: sequencing, timing, access, and the operational readiness of everything that goes live together
Own the internal resources our field teams reach for first, along with the operational side of enablement, including scheduling, speakers, and materials logistics
Develop and improve launch processes, playbooks, and operational frameworks that scale beyond any one launch
Own launch retrospectives, recurring product communications, and — when volume requires it — launch materials themselves

Have owned launch or release operations end to end, and been accountable for launches landing on time and in good shape
Have built or substantially improved a launch or release process
Treat process as a product — you care whether people adopt what you build, and you measure it
Background in product marketing, product operations, technical program management, and launch production all fit
Work well when priorities and timelines shift, and can keep a complex plan coherent as details change
Are effective at driving decisions across senior stakeholders without direct authority
Have a technical background with the ability to understand and communicate complex AI concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences
Write clearly, and can produce launch-ready material
Are energized by ambiguity and moving fast in a rapidly evolving market

Read more about what should I include in my federal resume at https://help.usajobs.gov/faq/application/documents/resume/what-to-include ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, as part of their application package, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, indicating the service member is otherwise eligible and will be discharged or released within 120 days from the date of submission..

A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service.

This "certification" must include your rank, dates of active duty service, type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable), and date any terminal leave will begin. It must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters.

Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible". Members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if they are on terminal leave.

Sobre a Área
Esta é uma posição de "Founding Member" dentro de uma das mais novas frentes de crescimento do QuintoAndar. Você será o primeiro profissional dedicado às operações jurídicas de um modelo de negócio inédito, e terá a oportunidade de construir o processo do zero. O Roll-up de Carteiras é o mais recente modelo de crescimento inorgânico do QuintoAndar.
A área de Ops Closing é o elo crítico entre a negociação comercial e o fechamento jurídico de cada deal. Sem ela, nenhuma aquisição se concretiza. Você será responsável por garantir que toda a documentação esteja correta, que os contratos sejam assinados dentro do prazo e que os pagamentos sejam executados conforme acordado, usando ferramentas de inteligência artificial para apoiar a análise jurídica.
Como a função é inédita na estrutura, você terá autonomia para desenhar os fluxos, criar as rotinas e estabelecer o padrão de operação que vai escalar com o crescimento da área.
Responsabilidades
Acompanhamento Documental: Acompanhar e cobrar o envio de documentação pelas imobiliárias, garantindo que todos os documentos necessários estejam completos antes da análise;
Due Diligence com IA: Realizar a análise de due diligence jurídica das imobiliárias e de seus contratos, utilizando um agente de inteligência artificial como ferramenta de apoio;
Interface de Alinhamento: Comunicar internamente e para a imobiliária o resultado da análise jurídica, sinalizando aprovações ou pendências;
Formalização de Contratos: Enviar os contratos para assinatura após a aprovação jurídica, acompanhando o processo de ponta a ponta até a conclusão;
Régua de Pagamentos: Programar e executar a régua de pagamentos de cada negociação fechada, viabilizando e operacionalizando os valores financeiros acordados;
Desenho de Processos: Desenhar e documentar os fluxos operacionais inéditos da área de Ops Closing, contribuindo diretamente para a criação de rotinas escaláveis;
Atuação Interfuncional: Atuar em sinergia com os times comercial, jurídico e de operações para garantir a fluidez do pipeline de aquisições.
Requisitos
Experiência em Backoffice: Experiência prévia indispensável em operações jurídicas ou backoffice — não é necessário ser advogado ou ter formação em Direito, mas é fundamental ter atuado com processos operacionais e suporte crítico;
Perfil Processual e Organizado: Capacidade demonstrada de gerenciar múltiplos deals simultaneamente, mantendo alto rigor com prazos, controles de documentos e follow-ups;
Autonomia de Nível B4: Senioridade e senso de dono para executar as próprias tarefas com independência, proatividade e sem necessidade de microgestão;
Resiliência e Conforto com Ambiguidade: Facilidade para transitar em ambientes em construção, lidando com processos que ainda estão sendo desenhados e estruturados;
Comunicação Assertiva: Excelente habilidade de comunicação escrita e verbal para interagir com parceiros externos (imobiliárias) e stakeholders internos de diferentes níveis;
Mentalidade Digital: Familiaridade ou total disposição para aprender a operar novas tecnologias e ferramentas de inteligência artificial aplicadas à análise de documentos.
Diferenciais
Experiência anterior em Closing Ops ou áreas correlatas em fintechs, imobiliárias, fundos de investimento ou empresas com histórico de M&A / Asset Deals;
Vivência profunda com análise de contratos, due diligence ou processos de compra e venda de ativos;
Experiência prévia em startups ou ambientes corporativos de alto crescimento, onde os processos são construídos paralelamente à execução da operação.

What this job can offer you
You will own and improve the platforms Customer Experience runs on: Zendesk, Vitally, and the integrations that connect them to the rest of the stack.

You will see work through from scoping to production and ongoing ownership: testing changes, communicating with affected teams, documenting what you ship, and keeping platforms reliable as requirements grow.

Automation experience in CX: low/no-code tools (Zapier, platform-native automations, or similar) and workflows that hold up in production.
Practical familiarity with AI in support and success operations: agent assist, workflow automation, triage or routing helpers, or knowledge-backed tools. Comfort with APIs, webhooks, and integration patterns; able to partner with engineering on harder problems.
Depth in Zendesk or a comparable support platform. Vitally or similar Customer Success platform experience is a strong plus. Willingness to work across more than one system in the stack.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Reporting into Partner Operations & Systems within Partner Experience, this role is the operations generalist behind the partner program — an ecosystem growing quickly, with volume growing faster and an operational layer still being designed.
The role has two anchors: intake — owning the front door for new process requests and building the intake process itself — and flexibility, serving as the generalist allocated to the most pressing operational issue at the time. You'll serve as the central hub for partner experience, working cross-functionally with Finance, RevOps, Sales, Enablement, Product, and Legal to ensure seamless execution of partnership strategy.

Own intake for new process requests: triage, scope, and prioritize needs across the partner organization and decide what gets built
Design new partner operations processes from zero to one: stand up the workflow, documentation, and requirements, and iterate with data
Build new AI automations with Claude: create and run Claude-powered automations and AI workflows across partner operations, taking them from prototype to production and improving them with use
Take on special operations projects: join small cross-functional teams on priority initiatives
Run the process and data side of registrations, referrals, incentives, applications, and onboarding, keeping the data decision-grade
Encode program policy in the systems: work with program owners so rules are enforced by systems, and own data hygiene for the partner record of truth
Enable partners and internal teams: build the guidance partners, Partner Managers, and Account Executives need for new initiatives
Collaborate across go-to-market: partner with Sales, Finance, Enablement, Marketing, and Revenue Operations to stay aligned with the business
Measure what matters: establish service levels and report on volume, cycle time, and the metrics that show what to fix next

Strong project management ability with experience influencing cross-functional operational initiatives
Hands-on experience creating AI workflows with Claude or similar tools, and comfort running and improving them at operational volume

Analytical mindset with the ability to derive actionable insights from complex datasets

Experience with partner or channel program design, including tiering and program benefits
Hands-on Salesforce experience, including reporting, data imports, and workflow configuration
A track record of standing up operational processes, service levels, and reporting from scratch
Experience on a tiger team or task force assembled to solve high-priority problems quickly

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains.

Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.
How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles.

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
Come work with us!

Who We Are
Imprint helps the world's best brands grow the lifetime value of their customers. We started with co-branded credit cards and rebuilt them to be smarter, more rewarding, and brand-first.

We partner with companies like Crate & Barrel, Rakuten, , H-E-B, Fetch, and Shell to launch modern credit programs that deepen loyalty, unlock savings, and drive growth. But the card is just the beginning.

We combine advanced payments infrastructure, intelligent underwriting, and deep customer data to create delightful and personalized experiences for members as well as efficient and profitable relationships for our brand partners.

Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank.
In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Imprint is the modern alternative: flexible, embeddable, and built for how people actually pay today. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.

As Fraud Operations Manager , you will own the day-to-day operations of Imprint 's fraud operations team, ensuring consistency, compliance, and quality across internal specialists and an outsourced BPO workforce. This is a hands-on people management role with direct accountability for team performance, SOP integrity, and vendor oversight as the team scales rapidly.
You will act as the operational backbone of fraud ops — closing gaps between what the process says and what agents actually do, and building systems that scale rather than just managing queues.
What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days
All team leads have structured coaching, guidance, and feedback in place, with productivity and QA measurements actively tracked
SOP gaps are identified, documented, and on a clear path to bank compliance sign-off
BPO (Ubiquity) QA scorecard is accurate, current, and measuring vendor performance against defined standards
Consistency across a team of 49 BPO agents and 22 specialists is meaningfully improved
Established as a trusted escalation point for fraud operations across the team

Own full-cycle people management for fraud operations, including team leads, internal specialists, and BPO vendor workforce
Drive SOP development, gap identification, and compliance approval processes to ensure all procedures are documented, current, and bank-approved
Manage the BPO relationship — maintain QA scorecards, hold vendors accountable to performance standards, and coach vendor agents directly
Partner with fraud strategy on workflow changes and emerging fraud trends without acting as a blocker
Serve as the escalation backstop for fraud operations issues and always bring a recommendation when raising a problem
Balance fraud prevention with user experience — treat false positives as a real cost, not just a fraud metric
Use data and operational insight to identify bottlenecks and drive process improvements
Build systems and processes that scale with rapid team growth

At OpenAI, our User Safety & Risk Operations (USRO) team helps protect our products and users from abuse, fraud, safety risks, and other forms of misuse. We translate real-world user and operational signals into timely decisions, practical interventions, and improvements to our products and systems.
This role will take on new, ambiguous, or underdeveloped operational risks and help mature them into scalable capabilities. We work across USRO and partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Product Policy, Legal, Safety, Support, and external vendors or partnership stakeholders.

We are seeking a Senior Operations Analyst to take on complex, ambiguous safety and risk problems and turn them into practical operational solutions that can scale.

This is a senior individual-contributor role for a versatile operator who is comfortable moving between queues, investigation, analysis, workflow design, hands-on execution, and cross-functional leadership. Depending on team needs, the role may focus on emerging-risk incubation, cloud deployment partnerships, or other new operational areas.
You will be expected to move quickly, work hands-on, and create structure without waiting for perfect requirements or a large support team. The work starts with the problem, not a prescribed process.

You may investigate unstructured user signals, stand up a lightweight workflow, build an AI-assisted tool, improve an existing operation, or help a new launch become operationally ready. The goal is to produce durable systems that other people can run, not simply complete a series of individual tasks.
The portfolio will change with company priorities and may span established harm areas, emerging-risk incubation, cloud deployments and partnerships, device safety, or new product launches. Some hires may focus primarily on cloud deployment operations, including launch readiness, partner coordination, safety workflows, and operational monitoring.

You will typically own a small number of high-impact problems at a time and will be expected to judge what needs to be built, what can stay lightweight, and when the work is ready to scale, transfer, or stop.
Location / work model: San Francisco, CA; hybrid, 3 days/week in-office.
Please note: This role may involve exposure to sensitive or concerning content. Strong discretion, good judgment, and resilience are essential.
In This Role, You Will
Take ownership of ambiguous, high-priority safety and risk problems: define the problem, gather the right evidence, choose a practical path, drive execution, and close the loop.
Analyze structured and unstructured data, both quantitative and qualitative. This may include user reports, case narratives, conversations, escalations, and operational metrics to identify patterns, risks, and the highest-leverage interventions.
Build and test lightweight workflows, tools, automations, and decision aids that improve speed, quality, and consistency, then iterate based on real-world use.
Turn one-off insights and manual work into scalable operating mechanisms without adding unnecessary process or complexity.
Lead sensitive investigations, incident response, or launch-readiness work, including safety workflows, human review, escalation paths, partner coordination, and operational monitoring for product launches or cloud deployments.
Work directly with cross-functional and external partners to clarify ownership, resolve operational gaps, and turn incomplete signals into clear recommendations and decisions.
Measure whether the work is improving outcomes—such as quality, speed, coverage, operator effort, or risk reduction—and adjust quickly when it is not.
Help junior operators build judgment and independence through coaching, calibration, and reusable tools.
You Might Thrive in This Role If You
Have 8+ years of experience in trust and safety operations, investigations, incident response, product operations, technical program management, or another high-judgment, data-heavy operational field.
Have a track record as a scrappy generalist who can enter an unfamiliar problem, learn quickly, and deliver with limited structure or support.
Are highly data savvy, including the ability to make sense of messy qualitative or unstructured information and combine it with quantitative evidence.
Are technically fluent and hands-on with AI tools, dashboards, and data tooling, and can build or prototype practical solutions without waiting for a dedicated technical team.
Operate independently, make clear tradeoffs, and maintain momentum as priorities and requirements change.
Think in systems: you look beyond the immediate task and build approaches that can be repeated, measured, and operated by others.
Exercise strong judgment in sensitive situations involving user impact, policy, legal risk, technical constraints, and business priorities.
Communicate clearly and directly, especially in writing, and can drive decisions across teams without formal authority.

Experience in trust and safety, fraud, product safety, integrity, or another adversarial or high-severity risk domain.
Experience moving a new or immature workflow from early investigation into stable, scaled operations.
Experience supporting cloud platforms or deployment partnerships, enterprise products, product launches, connected devices, or other technically complex programs. Direct cloud experience is a plus, not a requirement.
Familiarity with SQL, lightweight scripting, no-code tools, workflow automation, or AI-assisted development.
Experience with vendor operations, quality programs, calibrations, or distributed operational teams.

This is Amplitude's first People Team hire in India, and we're being deliberate about who we bring in first.
People Operations is at an inflection point. A lot of what takes hours today—HR tickets, Workday updates, onboarding tasks—will be handled by AI-assisted workflows in the near future. We're building toward that now, and this role is part of that foundation.

About Zip
Zip is the AI platform for enterprise procurement — built for humans and agents working together. By orchestrating procurement across teams, tools, and suppliers with the help of AI agents, companies can secure the resources they need to innovate faster than ever before.
The world’s most influential enterprises trust Zip, including T-Mobile, OpenAI, AMD, Mars, Dollar Tree, and more. Together they’ve saved over $8 billion and processed over $500 billion in spend. Zip’s team includes product leaders from Apple, Airbnb, and Meta, as well as former procurement leaders from United Health, Sanofi, MGM Resorts, Discover, and NASA.
Backed by Adams Street, Alkeon, BOND, CRV, DST, Tiger Global, and Y Combinator, Zip has raised $371 million, most recently at a $2.2 billion valuation and has been recognized by Forbes Fintech 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, Inc. Best in Business, and LinkedIn Top Startups.

As a member of Zip’s GTM Strategy & Operations team, you’ll be a key partner to Solution Engineering, Sales, Marketing, and the broader executive team - driving strategic planning, operational execution, and analytical rigor across our revenue engine. This team sits at the intersection of go-to-market execution, company strategy, and systems - giving you a unique seat at the table to shape the trajectory of the business.
You'll partner with Global Solutions Engineering leadership to bring structure to a fast-scaling SE org: standardizing how SEs engage across the deal cycle and driving the cross-functional collaboration with surrounding teams that makes that engagement work in practice.
You'll keep SE capability aligned to a fast-evolving product portfolio — shaping enablement and GTM strategy so a growing team can demo, scope, and defend what's shipping.

Own SE operations for the org: Lead day-to-day operations and long-term planning — the capacity and coverage model, hiring and ramp planning against open headcount, comp plan design, metrics, reporting, and "whatever it takes."
Act as a strategic thought partner: Be the go-to partner for SE leadership and execs - whether it's solving complex problems, framing key decisions, or bringing structure to ambiguity.
Drive GTM cadence and accountability: Run the operating rhythm - owning coverage and staffing reviews, pipeline/deal reviews, QBRs, and leadership syncs. You'll push velocity, track outcomes, and ensure every meeting drives impact.
Lead cross-functional execution: Work across SE, Sales, Marketing, CS, Product, and Finance to drive strategic initiatives forward - bringing a GTM perspective to company-wide efforts and ensuring alignment across teams.
Build with data : Use SQL, spreadsheets, and BI tools to structure analysis, validate assumptions, and uncover insights that improve GTM execution and drive growth.
Own special projects: From coverage model design to GTM enablement to redefining our POC motion - you’ll own critical, high-impact workstreams that move the business forward.

8+ years of experience in sales strategy, revenue operations, presales/solutions engineering operations, consulting, investing, or a similar high-performance environment.
Strong analytical and modeling skills - you're fluent in Excel/Sheets and can write SQL or are willing to learn.
Deep understanding of GTM motions and technical sales cycles, with battle-tested views on SE coverage ratios, POC/technical win rates, demo environment strategy, and capacity planning.
Experience working closely with GTM systems like Salesforce, Gong, and PreSales platforms
Excellent written and verbal communication - you can structure thinking clearly, write concise memos, and present to executives with confidence.
Attention to detail - you go deep on problems, sweat the edge cases, and set the quality bar high.
High bias for action - you move fast, think in tradeoffs, and find a way forward when others see blockers.
Technically inclined — you're not afraid of Salesforce Flows, brittle validation rules, or stitching together data across systems.
A collaborative mindset — you're opinionated but open to all perspectives, and you know how to drive alignment across stakeholders.
A proven operator — you've managed large, ambiguous projects that required both strategic thinking and tactical execution.

You will report to the Global Head of Operations and partner closely with Product, Sales, Finance, and Engineering. You will own the full loop: identify the opportunity, design the solution, deploy it with AI and automation tooling, and measure the outcome.

Design, deploy, and iterate on AI-powered workflows using tools like Claude Code/Codex, n8n, and other LLM APIs to do things that weren’t possible before and replace manual, repetitive, or error-prone processes.

Serve as the internal expert on AI tooling for operations — evaluating new tools, sharing what works, and building the internal playbook on how Clara uses AI.
Identify data gaps and work with Engineering to create the instrumentation or pipelines needed to power better operational decisions.
Document processes clearly so that what you build can be maintained, improved, and handed off — not just understood by you.

We're looking for a high-energy, detail-oriented and hands-on individual to join the Revenue Team as a Manager, Revenue Operations. This role will be based in our Palo Alto, CA office and will support the execution and scaling of revenue operations in a high-growth, multi-product environment. This is a highly visible individual contributor role with significant ownership across revenue close, technical accounting, and cross-functional initiatives.
This is a great opportunity to join and grow with a strong accounting team at a high growth, enterprise software company!
The Revenue team is an extremely visible, high-performing team, ultimately responsible for accurate financial reporting of revenue. The team is responsible for managing the monthly close, contract negotiation and documentation, and determining appropriate accounting treatment for our product offerings.

Additionally, this team is responsible for designing and maintaining controls over reporting of revenue and assisting in quarterly revenue forecasting activities. This role will report directly to the Senior Manager of Revenue.
We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in Palo Alto for our hybrid working model.
Position Expectations
Participate in month-end close activities comprising various revenue analyses, booking JEs, account reconciliations and revenue recognition
Analyze sales transactions within the Company’s ERP systems to ensure accuracy of data and integrity of revenue schedules, inclusive of revenue allocations
Review and validate all revenue streams for appropriate revenue treatments
Review contract write-ups and provide guidance on revenue treatment under ASC 606 and related financial reporting requirements to ensure appropriate revenue recognition
Experience establishing, maintaining, and reviewing standalone selling price ranges and methodologies
Manage the execution of quarterly reviews and year-end financial audits by external auditors
Provide functional oversight to Revenue Analysts, including reviewing work and offering guidance to support growth and development
Assist in the review and delivery of executive-level analytics and revenue disclosures by analyzing complex data sets, identifying trends, anomalies, and underlying drivers, and applying sound judgment to translate findings into actionable insights
Work cross-functionally with key internal business partners, such as OTC and FP&A on ongoing initiatives
Assist with special projects and ad hoc requests as required

Bachelor's degree in Accounting (CPA preferred) with at least 8+ years of experience in a similar role at public, high-growth SaaS or technology company
Prior experience with revenue operations, revenue recognition and reconciliation processes including working with sales data, customer contracts and new product offerings
Working knowledge of ASC 606, including application of SaaS and usage-based revenue models.
Proficiency in MS Excel and working with large volumes of data
Knowledge of ERP and CRM systems (NetSuite, Salesforce)
Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills
Acute attention to detail and well-developed organization
Excellent time management skills and ability to work in a fast-paced environment
Ability to take ownership of complex revenue areas, influence cross-functional partners, and independently drive projects to completion
Must be self-motivated, flexible and deadline-oriented
Outstanding interpersonal, communication, and business partnering skills with demonstrated ability to work cross functionally at various levels within the company
Success Measures
A successful candidate must have the ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving, global environment as well as have experience and a strong interest in revenue operation processes
In 30 days, a successful candidate will have become familiar with our business, product offerings, and revenue streams
In 3 to 6 months, you’ll have become familiar with our internal systems, operational workflows and accounting close tasks assigned to you and would be performing them independently
In 6 to 9 months, you’ll have established relationships with key business partners such as Billing/OTC, FP&A and would be working directly with them as and when issues arise

Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations.

At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy.

Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

The Sr. Business Operations Manager is a strategic partner to the leadership of Samsara’s Global Support organization, driving operational excellence and enabling data-informed decision-making at scale. This role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution, supporting senior leadership with the insights, communications, and operational frameworks needed to run and grow the business effectively.
This role owns the annual operating plan and the operating cadence that measures performance against it.

On the planning side, you will own the capacity, headcount, and cost model that connects support volume, productivity, AI deflection, and staffing assumptions into a defensible operating plan — and act as the connective tissue between Support leadership, Workforce Management, and Finance.

On the business operations side, you will own the reporting and business review cadence for Customer Support, turning a wide set of operational metrics into a clear narrative about what is happening, why, and what leadership should do about it.
This is a high-autonomy role for a builder. You will take ambiguous, loosely scoped problems: a cost target, a capacity gap, an unexplained trend, and return with structured analysis, a defensible model, and a recommendation leaders can act on.

You will operate credibly with senior stakeholders across Support, Finance, and People, influence without direct authority, and use modern AI tools every day to work at a level of speed and rigor that would not otherwise be possible.

Success in this role looks like leaders making better decisions faster, with a plan and a set of numbers everyone trusts.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.

You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.

Own the annual operating plan (AOP) for the Support organization end to end: building and maintaining the capacity, headcount, and cost model that translates volume forecasts, productivity, AI deflection, and staffing assumptions into a defensible operating plan and budget.
Model and pressure-test the strategic levers available to the business: headcount and vendor/BPO mix, cost to serve, deflection and automation impact, service level and coverage tradeoffs — and bring leadership clear recommendations with quantified impact and stated assumptions.
Own the Customer Support business review cadence (monthly and quarterly reviews) end to end: metric definition and data validation, executive narrative and insight, and follow-through on the decisions and actions that come out of it.
Build and maintain the reporting frameworks and metric definitions leaders run the business on — productivity, cost to serve, CSAT, time to resolution, deflection — and make them self-serve so managers can answer their own questions.
Partner with Support leaders on the operating programs that turn plan into behavior, including productivity and incentive program design, capacity allocation, and operational improvement initiatives that measurably improve efficiency and customer experience.
Leverage AI tools (e.g., Claude) and self-service data capabilities on a day-to-day basis to accelerate modeling, analysis, narrative generation, and reporting — and raise the bar for how the broader operations team applies them.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

10+ years of experience in business operations, strategic finance/FP&A, management consulting, strategy, or a related field.
Bachelor’s degree from a 4-year accredited university.
Experience owning an annual operating plan, capacity plan, or equivalent multi-quarter planning process for a large organization or function.
Demonstrated experience building and owning complex operating or financial models (headcount, capacity, and cost) that senior leaders make decisions from.
Experience owning a recurring executive business review cadence (e.g., MBR/QBR) end to end, including metric definitions, narrative, and follow-through.
Demonstrated ability to build executive-level presentations and strategic communications that convey a clear, compelling narrative.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to independently source, interpret, and synthesize large and imperfect datasets to support decision-making, including familiarity with data tools (e.g., Tableau, Looker, SQL, Databricks) for self-serve analytics.
Comfort and previous experience using AI tools for analysis, modeling, content generation, and workflow automation.
Experience working cross-functionally and influencing senior stakeholders without direct authority.
High degree of independence and intellectual curiosity: able to take a loosely defined problem and return with structured, rigorous thinking and actionable recommendations.
Experience in or with a customer support, technical support, or service delivery organization operating at scale across multiple sites and a vendor/BPO mix.

Criamos um ambiente de trabalho para você prosperar em todas as dimensões da sua vida. A gente faz isso por meio de benefícios bem pensados, recursos para o bem-estar emocional e uma cultura que empodera cada pessoa a realmente se conectar com seu papel aqui e ser dona dele, balanceando isso com o próprio bem-estar.
Nosso programa de benefícios flexíveis ajuda você a customizá-los de acordo com as suas necessidades!

WELLHUB: Plano Gold+ gratuito, com acesso a milhares de academias e estúdios, programas fitness digitais e recursos online para meditação, nutrição, suporte de saúde mental, rotina de sono e mais. Você também pode adicionar até 3 familiares ao seu plano, garantindo que quem mais importa para você tenha acesso a bem-estar.
WELLZ: Um recurso único e completo para o bem-estar mental. O Wellz oferece jornadas personalizadas que combinam sessões semanais de terapia cognitivo-comportamental (52 por ano) e conteúdo à demanda.
SAÚDE E CUIDADO: Plano de saúde, plano odontológico e seguro de vida.
TRABALHO FLEXÍVEL: Com o regime de trabalho que prioriza flexibilidade, a gente oferece vagas híbridas e remotas, para que tenha a liberdade de trabalhar do jeito que funciona melhor para você. Quando você entrar no Wellhub, também pode usar o nosso reembolso de home office para montar o seu escritório em casa!
DESCANSO REMUNERADO: Se desconectar e recarregar as energias é muito importante. Por isso, oferecemos férias após 6 meses de trabalho + 3 dias de folga por ano + 1 dia de folga a cada ano na empresa (somando até 5 dias) + 1 dia de folga no mês do seu aniversário!
LICENÇA PARENTAL REMUNERADA: Receber um novo membro na família é um dos momentos mais especiais da vida. Queremos que cada pessoa colaboradora possa estar presente de verdade e aproveite esse tempo em família. Por isso, oferecemos licença parental 100% remunerada a todos os novos pais. Quem dá à luz também tem direito à licença estendida (Empresa Cidadã) e a um período de adaptação (ramp-back), em que pode trabalhar meio-período até se ajustar à nova rotina.
DESENVOLVIMENTO PROFISSIONAL: Tenha acesso a plataformas de aprendizado (incluindo linguístico), participe de sessões interativas e explore nossas oportunidades internas. No seu estágio, você também vai desenvolver um projeto todo seu, baseado na área e suas especialidades e ter apadrinhamento para ajudar no seu estágio. No Wellhub, a gente foca em aprendizado e feedback contínuos para apoiar seu caminho em direção ao sucesso – tanto pessoal quanto profissional.
CULTURA: Você vai se juntar a uma equipe de pessoas dedicadas, que se unem para romper limites, apoiar umas às outras e criar impacto duradouro no bem-estar corporativo. Nós vencemos em conjunto, cultivando relações de confiança por meio de comunicação transparente e de uma cultura em que cada perspectiva importa. Entenda mais sobre nossos valores e cultura.

Health can’t wait .

Alan exists to end the wait.
Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.
So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.
We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture . We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.
Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 800+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

As we anchor our Insurance position, diversify our offering with health and well-being related services in 4 different countries (France, Belgium, Spain and Canada), our operations are increasingly complex and our challenges ahead have never been as exciting!
Being an Ops at Alan means joining a team of 50+ talented, committed and passionate Ops across our countries , with a lot of interactions with Engineering, Product, Care and many other teams at Alan.

📍 Join Alan’s Operations team in Lyon
The Operations Coordinator works on a specific subset of services we deliver (eg. claim reimbursement, fraud, clinic to name a few) .

s.h: Their core responsibilities (+- 70/80% of the time) are to
s.t:
Run our Insurance or Health services processes - that's why we call them Ops Runners internally 😉
Ensure the day-to-day follow up and monitoring of our operations
Flag risks and opportunities

Operating our processes: performing tasks like invoicing or claims treatment, growing and managing our network of providers, supporting internal teams (live and through documentation)
Contributing to the definition & owning the best monitoring scheme to track volumes/efficiency/SLAs, and identify risks and areas of improvement, internally or with our service providers
Supervising partnerships (e.g. teleconsultation, claim operators) , participating in the negotiation rounds, daily communication to ensure business continuity
Performing controls on our daily operations to make sure the correct decisions were made and to identify training needs (internally as well as externally)
Escalating feedback, helping to prioritise and supporting initiatives to make our processes and services more delightful and efficient
Next to running and monitoring our operations, you implement continuous improvements to our processes (+-20/30% of the time) . ⭐️ Our Run organisation ⭐️
Our Operations Coordinators or Ops Runners are organized in pools (3-7 runners) who are collectively responsible for running their scope. Examples of topics are:
Alan therapy: members can book a therapy session with psychologists. You maintain smooth relationships with our psychologists, ensure therapy demand matches the supply and contribute to several steps of their lifecycle at Alan (hiring, onboarding, invoicing, supporting booking management etc).

About Wayflyer
Today's small businesses need a capital provider that keeps pace with their growth ambitions. Traditional financing options are slow, cumbersome and often out of reach. That's why we built Wayflyer.
Our technology allows us to assess businesses in minutes, generate financing offers that reflect their growth potential and send funds in as little as 24 hours. To date, we've deployed over $6bn to thousands of businesses worldwide, backed by Tier 1 banks like J.P. Morgan.
You'll be collaborating with ambitious colleagues from around the world. We have offices in Dublin, London, New York, Charlotte, Berlin and Sydney.
The challenge
RevOps at Wayflyer is a team of builders. We're not just looking for people who can spot what's broken and flag it, that skill matters and we have great people who do it well. We're looking for people who also have the technical range to build the fix themselves, independently, without waiting on someone else's roadmap.
We sit at the epicenter of an exceptionally fast-growing business running across multiple channels and partners, and it's our job to make sure the systems underneath that growth have the ability to scale. This role is for a builder who wants to see the impact of their work fast, ideally in seconds, while still thinking several steps ahead so today's quick fix doesn't turn into next year's technical debt. We want people who enjoy the instant feedback loop just as much as the long game.
What you'll actually do
Integrations & Technical Ownership: Build, maintain and improve the systems, internal automations and integrations that make our sales and CS teams faster and more effective, from the ground up.
AI-Native Systems: Build, deploy and continuously sharpen AI-native workflows and agents that augment how Sales, CS and the wider Revenue org work, not just automate around the edges.
Data, Analytics & Problem Solving: Use self-sourced data to diagnose what's actually broken, run root cause analysis, and build the fix yourself, then measure it against real KPIs and keep iterating.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Project Ownership: Work directly with Sales, Partnerships, Marketing and Finance to turn half-formed requirements into systems that actually solve the problem.
Revenue Data Hygiene: Own regular audits, deduplication, enrichment and the process fixes that keep our data usable across every system that touches it.
Driving Operational Excellence: Spot inefficiencies before anyone asks you to, prioritise ruthlessly, and build the automated solutions that let the function scale without adding headcount.
What this role could turn into
This function sits at the intersection of Revenue, Marketing, Finance, Data and Engineering, so you'll get exposure most people spend years angling for. People who do this well tend to move toward GTM strategy, GTM engineering, product roles, and beyond. The sky is the limit.
Who thrives here
You're an AI-native builder who thinks in scale, not one-off fixes, and gets uncomfortable when you spot a manual workaround. You're just as comfortable pairing with Engineering as you are in the room with Sales leadership, translating one for the other without losing anything in the middle.

You run towards the hardest, messiest problems, you don't wait for permission, and you don't need a fully-scoped brief before you start. You're always watching what the best GTM teams are building, and you'd rather pitch a bold idea than ship another incremental tweak.
We hire for range
3+ years in RevOps, MarOps, consulting or similar, but tenure isn't the point, trajectory is. Whatever your background, you're an AI-native builder with strong business acumen and a sharp eye for the difference between a good customer experience and a bad one.
You bring fluency in Python (or Node) and SQL, hands-on experience configuring HubSpot and its developer suite, and comfort with automation platforms like Zapier, Pipedream, n8n or UiPath.

You've likely configured CPQ, CLM, sales engagement or customer-success platforms before, and just as importantly, you've driven adoption of something you built, not just shipped it and walked away. Extra credit if you've built and deployed AI agents, integrated AI/LLM-based solutions into existing workflows, or built automated pipelines end to end.
Location and working policy
📍 Dublin or London, Hybrid
The good stuff
25 days off, plus public holidays. Private healthcare, life insurance, and pension. Equity, because you should own a piece of what you're building. Generous parental leave for primary and secondary caregivers. 60 days a year to work abroad from wherever you want.

We're seeking a Customer Operations Manager, to own the build, quality, and ongoing maintenance of our Gainsight content— including playbooks, health rules, and human handoff alerting logic. This role sits at the intersection of customer marketing and RevOps, translating lifecycle strategy into scalable, reliably-functioning CSP content.

You'll be the Customer Marketing content builder in Gainsight, ensuring every playbook is built to specification, monitoring and reporting on their success to lifecycle managers and CS counterparts.

5+ years of hands-on experience building and maintaining playbooks, rules, and workflows in Gainsight CSP (required)
Demonstrated experience designing alerting or handoff logic between marketing/lifecycle systems and human teams (CS, Sales, RevOps)
Strong systems-thinking mindset with a track record of building for scale — able to anticipate where logic will break as volume, segments, or use cases multiply
Experience partnering closely with RevOps or CS Ops on shared data models, CRM integrations, and cross-system dependencies
Rigorous approach to QA and documentation; comfortable establishing process and standards where none exist
Familiarity with customer health scoring, lifecycle segmentation, or adoption frameworks strongly preferred
Analytical mindset with the ability to troubleshoot logic issues independently and communicate root cause clearly to non-technical stakeholders
Excellent cross-functional communication and project management skills; able to manage multiple concurrent build requests and competing priorities
B2B SaaS experience preferred; customer marketing, customer success, or RevOps background all relevant

Own end-to-end build of Gainsight CSP playbooks — from requirements gathering with lifecycle marketing, CS, and RevOps stakeholders through configuration, testing, and launch
Design and maintain human handoff alerting logic in partnership with RevOps, ensuring the right signals route to the right owners at the right time with minimal false positives or missed triggers
Establish and enforce build quality standards (naming conventions, documentation, QA/testing protocols, version control) so playbooks scale cleanly as new use cases and teams are added
Monitor and report on live playbooks and alerts on an ongoing basis, proactively identifying and resolving breakage, logic drift, or data issues before they impact customers
Partner with Lifecycle lead and RevOps on data architecture and system dependencies (CRM, health score inputs, product usage data) that feed CSP logic, flagging upstream issues that affect playbook accuracy
Build and maintain internal documentation of playbook logic, ownership, and change history to support auditability and smooth handoffs as the team scales
Continuously evaluate the playbook portfolio for redundancy, performance, and opportunities for consolidation or optimization as lifecycle and adoption strategy evolves
Serve as Customer Marketing Gainsight subject matter expert, advising lifecycle marketing and CS stakeholders on capabilities and constraints when building new initiatives

Expert Insights, which spans AlphaSense’s Expert Transcript Library and 1x1 Call Services offerings, delivers a new and transformative form of market intelligence content.

Through transcripts covering thousands of companies, it captures the unfiltered views and insights of business operators in the trenches, interviewed by professional investors who drill into key questions on what’s truly important about a company at each moment in time.

AlphaSense’s library of over 140,000 transcripts is the market’s largest, covering all sectors of the economy, with thousands more published each month.

Expert Insights is quickly becoming a table-stakes solution for institutional investors to choose the right companies to invest in while gaining rapid adoption among all other consumers of market intelligence from sell-side research and banking, consultancies, and large corporations.

The Directed Content Team is an integral part of the Expert Insights group, generating thousands of calls each quarter on high-value and strategic content targets - ensuring that the AlphaSense Expert Transcript Library delivers comprehensive coverage to our users.

The Directed Content team is responsible for identifying, recruiting, and onboarding the best possible experts from around the world based on the targets and topics we are looking to generate content against - ensuring that the interviews with those experts are of the highest-possible quality and relevance.

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Generated Content - Directed Content Operations Managers oversee our Directed Content research pods.

Operations Managers are accountable for the overall performance of the research pods under their purview - motivating, managing, and supporting a diverse team of bi-lingual Analysts in the delivery of high-quality, relevant content against our Directed Content volume and coverage goals.

Natural people leaders, our Operations Managers are responsible for cultivating the talent on their team, bringing out the best in our employees through coaching, goal setting, and the delivery of clear and actionable feedback.

Operations Managers are also process optimizers, identifying bottlenecks in Analyst workflows that slow production or lead to wasted efforts, and addressing them in ways that ensure the delivery of high-quality and relevant content to the library.

Operations Managers work hand-in-hand with our Project Managers and Sector Leads to deliver timely, relevant content

Inspiring leader: You are deeply invested in Directed Content’s mission and vision of delivering high-quality, relevant insights to our customers - and are adept at connecting your team and their efforts to that mission, fostering a sense of ownership and meaning
People manager: You have deep experience setting performance and professional development goals, and a successful track record in motivating, coaching, supporting, and holding individuals accountable in achieving those goals
Team builder: You know how to build culture and support infrastructure that brings individual contributors together and enables them achieve their greatest collective potential
Entrepreneurial: You are passionate about the development of teams, people, and processes and are motivated to drive the success of Directed Content and Expert Insights
Metrics minded: You have a demonstrated track record of setting relevant KPIs to measure the success of both people and processes
Data driven: You have a proven ability to build dashboards and analysis to spot patterns in productivity and output that inform your day-to-day management of the team
Process innovator: You have a strong track record of building processes that drive scale and efficiency for your teams
Problem solver: You have a proven ability to identify the root cause of issues and roadblocks, and implement sustainable solutions
Skilled communicator: You’re able to leverage excellent oral and written communication skills to understand needs and drive alignment both with internal and external stakeholders

Manage a team of Directed Content Analysts aligned to sectors of coverage and structured in pods. The team will be partially comprised of bilingual Manadarin speakers.
Set and track performance KPIs for your team that balance output quality, relevance, and volume
Guide the professional development of Analysts under your supervision
Ensure overall library quality and relevance by partnering with Project Managers and Sector Leads to adjust research focus and sourcing strategies that support quality and relevance goals
Coordinate with Project Managers to define and update coverage territories based on evolving coverage goals and team capacity
Hire and onboard Analysts

Partner with Directed Content Enablement to design and maintain process documentation and knowledge resources for team
Partner with Director of Contributor Relations to ensure optimal Client Contributor coverage based on Directed Content coverage goals
Work closely with leadership and cross-functional teams to troubleshoot issues and devise process, systems, and workflow improvements for research pods
Review and approve expert rates over a fixed threshold - keeping average expert costs below $300 per call
